title: Main-Group Chemistry
full_title: Inorganic Chemistry of the Main-Group Elements
tagline: Periodic trends, bonding in main-group compounds, acids and bases, redox diagrams and the chemistry of the s- and p-block elements
summary: Inorganic chemistry studies all the elements and their compounds. This course explains the periodic trends and bonding models that organise main-group chemistry and the acid–base and redox principles behind its reactions, then surveys the chemistry of hydrogen, the s block and groups 13 to 18.

chapters.title: Periodic trends in the main-group elements
chapters.summary: Trends in size, ionisation energy, electronegativity and oxidation states across the s and p blocks, the inert-pair effect and diagonal relationships.

chapters.title: Structure and bonding in main-group compounds
chapters.summary: Hypervalent molecules, three-centre bonds, electron-deficient compounds and multiple bonding in the heavier elements.

chapters.title: Acids, bases and the HSAB principle
chapters.summary: The Brønsted acidity of oxides and oxoacids, Lewis acids and bases, hard and soft acids and bases, and non-aqueous solvents.

chapters.title: Redox chemistry and the extraction of elements
chapters.summary: Reduction potentials, Latimer, Frost and Pourbaix diagrams, disproportionation, and Ellingham diagrams for extracting metals from their ores.

chapters.title: Hydrogen and the s-block elements
chapters.summary: Hydrogen and its hydrides, the alkali and alkaline-earth metals, their compounds and their solutions in liquid ammonia.

chapters.title: Groups 13 and 14
chapters.summary: Boron and the boranes, aluminium, the allotropes of carbon, and silicon, silicates and silicones.

chapters.title: Groups 15 and 16
chapters.summary: Nitrogen and phosphorus, oxygen and sulfur, and their hydrides, oxides and oxoacids.

chapters.title: The halogens and the noble gases
chapters.summary: The halogens, interhalogen compounds and halogen oxoacids, and the compounds of the noble gases.
